summary:
AstroHealth OS is an autonomous deep-space health assessment and clinical decision support system built for Artemis lunar and Mars transit missions.

What we developed: An interactive aerospace medical suite featuring a holographic bio-digital twin, an autonomous clinical triage engine, a simulated ultrasound/retinal imaging lab with digital calipers, a psychomotor vigilance cognitive test (PVT-B), and gamified daily health tracking.

How it addresses the challenge: With 10-to-44-minute Earth communication delays making live flight surgeon support impossible in emergencies, AstroHealth OS acts as an onboard "virtual flight surgeon." It maps crew vitals to NASA’s five spaceflight hazards (R.I.D.G.E.) and recommends immediate hardware and medical countermeasures (like Chibis LBNP for fluid shifts and ARED resistive workouts for bone loss).

Why it is important: It enables medical self-sufficiency, prevents irreversible spaceflight conditions like permanent vision loss (SANS) and kidney stones, and protects crew survival far beyond Earth's orbit.
details:
AstroHealth OS is an autonomous deep-space medical suite and clinical decision support system built with TypeScript, React, SVG, HTML5 Canvas, and Web Audio API for Artemis lunar and Mars transit missions.

  • What it does: Acts as an onboard "virtual flight surgeon" featuring a holographic bio-digital twin, an autonomous triage engine, a simulated ultrasound/retinal imaging lab with digital calipers, a cognitive vigilance test (PVT-B), and gamified daily health quests ("AstroFit").
  • Benefits & Impact: Overcomes 10-to-44-minute Earth communication delays by enabling immediate, autonomous medical care. It catches critical spaceflight conditions early—such as vision-threatening fluid shifts (SANS), bone loss, and kidney stones—and pairs them with real flight countermeasures (like Chibis LBNP suits and ARED workouts) to keep crews safe and mission-ready.
  • Key Design Factors: Combines intuitive spatial visuals, synthesized audio alerts, and single-click workflows to reduce crew cognitive load during high-stress emergencies while strictly respecting spacecraft medical kit limits.
